messages.subject: Part 4 night-level, error_onset question
parts:
Hello all,
In the part 4 night-level summaries, there are three variables starting with "error_" (e.g., error_onset) that show the difference between, for example, the sleeponset and guider_onset. If I'm not using a sleep diary, and all my SPT are estimated using the HDCZA algorithm - then why are these different at all?  In other words: when not using a sleep diary, how are sleeponset and guider_onset estimated? why do they differ?

thank you,
Nicolle

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Part 4 night-level, error_onset question
parts:
Hello Nicolle,

This section from the package vignette should answer your question. Let me know if anything is unclear.

Once you have read that it should hopefully be clear that you are using the HDCZA algorithm as guider, because that is the default when no sleep diary is provided. Next, the somewhat unfortunate term 'error' refers to the difference between the HDCZA estimate which acts as a surrogate sleep log, and the final estimate which also looks at sustained inactivity bouts. 

Note to other - This only relates to the full report stored in the QC folder. For research I would recommend using the cleaned report instead. See: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/GGIR.html#564_Difference_between_cleaned_and_full_output

Best wishes,

Vincent
